sentences.en: Charles the Prince, girded boldly with gleaming arms, tamed this people through numerous blows and a thousand triumphs.
sentences.zh: 查理王子，身披闪亮的铠甲，英勇无畏，通过无数次的打击和千百次的胜利，驯服了这个民族。

sentences.en: He crushed it down and subjected it to himself with brandished sword.
sentences.zh: 他挥舞利剑，将其彻底粉碎，令其臣服于自己。

sentences.en: He dragged the battalions of those who in the depths of forests worshipped stock and stone into heavenly kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 他将那些在森林深处崇拜木石偶像的军队，拖入了天国。

sentences.en: Afterwards, he poured over with the salvation-bringing Jew of Baptism the untaught Saxons and sent them to the stars of heaven and led the new children of Christ into his hall.
sentences.zh: 随后，他用洗礼的救赎之水浇灌了那些未受教化的撒克逊人，将他们送往天上的星辰，并引领这些基督的新子民进入了他的殿堂。

sentences.en: So that was a fellow called Paulinus.
sentences.zh: 那个人叫保利努斯。

sentences.en: He was a scholar from northern Italy.
sentences.zh: 他是一位来自意大利北部的学者。

sentences.en: Lovely poem.
sentences.zh: 很棒的诗。

sentences.en: I think it's a banger.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这诗写得真带劲。

sentences.en: And Paulinus, not just a bishop, but a saint, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且保利努斯不仅是一位主教，还是一位圣人，汤姆。

sentences.en: He becomes one in due course, not when he's written that poem, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 说句公道话，他是在后来才成为圣人的，写那首诗的时候还不是。

sentences.en: But it's all in the future.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都是后话了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You get your sainthood partly as a reward for that beautiful poem.
sentences.zh: 你获得圣徒身份，在某种程度上也是对那首优美诗篇的奖赏。

sentences.en: Yes, like the poet laureate.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像桂冠诗人一样。

sentences.en: So he writes this poem in the year 777.
sentences.zh: 所以他在777年写下了这首诗。

sentences.en: And we are in the realm of Charlemagne, Charles the Great, warlord of the West, great king, great emperor, as we will discover as this story continues.
sentences.zh: 当时我们正处于查理曼——查理大帝的统治之下，他是西方的军阀、伟大的国王、伟大的皇帝，随着故事的深入，我们将会发现这一点。

sentences.en: So, Tom, give us a little bit of context.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，给我们讲讲背景吧。

sentences.en: Charlemagne has been joint king of the Frankish Empire for nine years with his brother, Carloman.
sentences.zh: 查理曼与他的兄弟卡洛曼共同统治法兰克帝国已经九年了。

sentences.en: But a terrible thing has happened to Carloman.
sentences.zh: 但卡洛曼发生了一件可怕的事。

sentences.en: Carloman had a nosebleed, as listeners will remember, and has died.
sentences.zh: 听众们可能还记得，卡洛曼流了鼻血，然后就去世了。

sentences.en: So Charlemagne is the last man standing.
sentences.zh: 所以查理曼成了最后留下来的人。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So give us a little bit of context.
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲背景吧。

sentences.en: We're in the aftermath of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于罗马帝国覆灭后的时期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Charles, he rules the Franks.
sentences.zh: 查理统治着法兰克人。

sentences.en: He's the son of Pepin, who's made himself king, getting rid of the Merovingian kings.
sentences.zh: 他是丕平的儿子，丕平通过废黜墨洛温王朝的国王，使自己成为了国王。

sentences.en: He's the grandson of Charles Martel, great warlord.
sentences.zh: 他是伟大的军阀查理·马特的孙子。

sentences.en: And Charles, in Latin, is Carolus.
sentences.zh: 查理在拉丁语中是Carolus。

sentences.en: And so the dynasty that Pepin has founded and that Charlemagne belongs to is known by historians as the Carolingian dynasty.
sentences.zh: 因此，丕平创立、查理曼所属的王朝，被历史学家称为加洛林王朝。

sentences.en: So Charles is top Carolingian.
sentences.zh: 所以查理是加洛林王朝的领袖。

sentences.en: He's top Frank.
sentences.zh: 他是法兰克人的领袖。

sentences.en: And to be honest, he's top guy in Europe because he has put the whole of the old heartlands of the Roman Empire in his shadow.
sentences.zh: 老实说，他是欧洲的头号人物，因为他将整个罗马帝国的旧核心地带都笼罩在了自己的阴影之下。

sentences.en: And he is now pushing eastwards.
sentences.zh: 他现在正向东扩张。

sentences.en: And that, I think, excellent poem that you read by Paul Anus, who in due course, as we said, will go on to become a saint.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，保利努斯——他后来会成为圣人——写的那首精彩的诗，我认为，

sentences.en: This is celebrating the conquest and the conversion of the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 这首诗是在歌颂对撒克逊人的征服与皈依。

sentences.en: And these were a pagan people on the eastern flank of the Frankish Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们是法兰克帝国东侧的一个异教民族。

sentences.en: Relations with the Franks had been terrible for ages and ages.
sentences.zh: 与法兰克人的关系长期以来一直非常糟糕。

sentences.en: They'd endlessly been kind of raiding Frankish lands, nicking their cattle, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们不断地袭击法兰克人的土地，偷走他们的牛，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And this had been a kind of grumbling cause of complaint under the Merovingians and then under the Carolingians.
sentences.zh: 在墨洛温王朝和后来的加洛林王朝统治下，这一直是一种令人不满的抱怨根源。

sentences.en: But Charlemagne, he's very much a guy for a radical solution.
sentences.zh: 但查理曼是一个倾向于采取激进解决方案的人。

sentences.en: And he's piling right in and saying,
sentences.zh: 他直接介入并说道：

sentences.en: OK, I'm not going to put up with this.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我不会再忍受这些了。”

sentences.en: I'm going to conquer them.
sentences.zh: “我要征服他们。”

sentences.en: So he had gone to war against them in 772.
sentences.zh: 于是他在772年对他们发动了战争。

sentences.en: So that's the year after he's become sole king.
sentences.zh: 那是他成为唯一国王后的第二年。

sentences.en: And this has lasted on and off for five years.
sentences.zh: 这场战争断断续续持续了五年。

sentences.en: And now it seems to Paul Anus that Charlemagne has succeeded in his aims, that the Saxons are conquered.
sentences.zh: 现在在保利努斯看来，查理曼已经实现了他的目标，撒克逊人已经被征服了。

sentences.en: It's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And so he salutes Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 于是他向查理曼致敬。

sentences.en: May God grant the Clement Prince as his reward for achieving such a victory, the sweet pastures of eternal life.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝赐予这位仁慈的王子永恒生命的甜蜜牧场，作为他取得如此胜利的奖赏。

sentences.en: It's all looking good for Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 查理曼的一切看起来都很顺利。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真不错。

sentences.en: So people who might be a little bit confused, these are Saxons in what is now Germany.
sentences.zh: 可能会有人感到困惑，这些撒克逊人是在现在的德国境内。

sentences.en: This is not Anglo-Saxon.
sentences.zh: 这并不是盎格鲁-撒克逊人。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Saxony.
sentences.zh: 是的，也就是萨克森地区。

sentences.en: Yeah, in Saxony.
sentences.zh: 是的，在萨克森。

sentences.en: So Lower Saxony.
sentences.zh: 也就是下萨克森州。

sentences.en: To give people a sort of sense, that's the northern bit of kind of Western Germany at this point.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念，那大约是现在德国西部的北部地区。

sentences.en: Though Saxony then...
sentences.zh: 虽然当时的萨克森……

sentences.en: Yeah, kind of below Denmark.
sentences.zh: 是的，就在丹麦下面。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Charlemagne, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那么查理曼，汤姆。

sentences.en: Charles the Great.
sentences.zh: 查理大帝。

sentences.en: He's a funny character, isn't he, Charlemagne?
sentences.zh: 查理曼是个很有趣的人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: Lots of people have heard of Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 很多人都听说过查理曼。

sentences.en: But I think it's fair to say that a lot of people know no more about him than his name.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，很多人除了他的名字之外，对他一无所知。

sentences.en: So he is a new figure.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个新的人物。

sentences.en: He is an entirely sui generis and exceptional figure in European history because he's different from all the warlords who've gone before him.
sentences.zh: 他在欧洲历史上是一个完全独一无二、非凡的人物，因为他与之前所有的军阀都不同。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: He's not radically different.
sentences.zh: 他并没有本质上的不同。

sentences.en: It's just that he is more impressive and he has more resources to draw on.
sentences.zh: 只是他更令人印象深刻，而且他拥有更多的资源可以利用。

sentences.en: And so therefore he can behave in a way that hasn't been seen in Western Europe for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 因此，他能够以一种西欧很久没有出现过的方式行事。

sentences.en: So Peter Brown, the great historian of late antiquity, says of Charlemagne that he was not a warrior chieftain in a fragile epic mode.
sentences.zh: 所以，晚期古代的伟大历史学家彼得·布朗说，查理曼不是那种脆弱史诗模式下的战士首领。

sentences.en: He trod with the heavy tread of a dominus, so a Roman lord, a lord of Roman determination, capable of deploying resources on an almost Roman scale.
sentences.zh: 他以统治者的沉重步伐行走，即一位罗马领主，一位具有罗马式决心的领主，有能力以近乎罗马的规模部署资源。

sentences.en: And these resources are preeminently military because he has inherited from Pepin and from his grandfather, Charles Martel, by far the most menacing war machine in Europe.
sentences.zh: 这些资源主要是军事上的，因为他从丕平和他的祖父查理·马特那里继承了欧洲迄今为止最可怕的战争机器。

sentences.en: But he adds to that some very, very kind of distinctive personal qualities.
sentences.zh: 但他还增加了一些非常、非常独特的个人品质。

sentences.en: So in the previous episode, we heard from Einhard, who was this very short scholar who wrote a biography of Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 在上一集中，我们听到了艾因哈德的讲述，他是一位身材非常矮小的学者，写了一部查理曼传记。

sentences.en: And Einhard summed up Charlemagne as having two particularly striking character traits.
sentences.zh: 艾因哈德总结说，查理曼有两个特别引人注目的性格特征。

sentences.en: He said that he had greatness of soul and a constant firmness of mind.
sentences.zh: 他说他有伟大的灵魂和始终如一的坚定意志。

sentences.en: And I guess you could, if you were not as prone to praising Charlemagne as Einhard was, you could say that these qualities correspond perhaps to having very broad horizons,
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你不像艾因哈德那样倾向于赞美查理曼，你可能会说这些品质对应的是拥有非常广阔的视野，

sentences.en: a capacity to see things on a very large scale, and also a capacity to take a very, very long view.
sentences.zh: 一种以宏大视角看待事物的能力，以及一种着眼于非常、非常长远的能力。

sentences.en: And to Einhard, these qualities remind him of perhaps the greatest of all Roman emperors, who is Augustus.
sentences.zh: 对艾因哈德来说，这些品质让他想起了也许是最伟大的罗马皇帝——奥古斯都。

sentences.en: And this is why Einhard models his biography on Suetonius' biography of Augustus.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么艾因哈德以苏埃托尼乌斯的《奥古斯都传》为蓝本撰写他的传记。

sentences.en: And there is something Roman about the approach that Charlemagne takes to the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 查理曼对待撒克逊人的方式确实有一些罗马色彩。

sentences.en: So anyone who knows how the Romans behaved to the Germans, or indeed to the Gauls when they conquered them, they are murderous in their response to perceived slights or insults.
sentences.zh: 任何了解罗马人如何对待德国人，或者在征服高卢人时如何对待他们的人都知道，他们对感知到的轻视或侮辱的反应是极其残暴的。

sentences.en: And certainly, Charlemagne's policy of outright conquest, we've got these kind of fractious barbarians, let's go and conquer them and pacify them.
sentences.zh: 当然，查理曼的彻底征服政策——我们有这些难缠的野蛮人，让我们去征服并平定他们。

sentences.en: That is a very Roman approach.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常罗马式的做法。

sentences.en: And there's an account from a chronicler describing Charlemagne's early campaigns against the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 有一位编年史家描述了查理曼早期对撒克逊人的战役。

sentences.en: And it will sound to people, I think, like the historians of Rome, describing the onslaught of the legionaries against the barbarian people.
sentences.zh: 我想，在人们听来，这就像罗马历史学家描述军团对野蛮民族的猛攻一样。

sentences.en: So this chronicler writes,
sentences.zh: 这位编年史家写道：

sentences.en: Charles devastated the lands of the Saxons with fire and sword and left them emptied of people.
sentences.zh: “查理用火与剑蹂躏了撒克逊人的土地，使那里人烟绝迹。”

sentences.en: And when he targets a particularly celebrated Saxon shrine, he's described as destroying it utterly and taking away all the gold and silver he found there.
sentences.zh: 当他瞄准一个特别著名的撒克逊神殿时，他被描述为将其彻底摧毁，并带走了他在那里发现的所有金银。

sentences.en: And I think even when we say the Saxons, that again is a Frankish formulation that reflects the tendency that the Romans had,
sentences.zh: 我认为即使当我们说“撒克逊人”时，那也是一种法兰克式的表述，反映了罗马人的一种倾向，

sentences.en: which was to kind of perceive pagan peoples, tribal peoples, peoples on the fringes of their civilization in terms that they would understand.
sentences.zh: 即以他们能理解的方式去感知异教民族、部落民族以及处于文明边缘的民族。

sentences.en: And of course, that's what the Romans had done to the Franks.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗马人当年也是这样对待法兰克人的。

sentences.en: And now the Franks are doing it to these people that they kind of bundle together as Saxons.
sentences.zh: 而现在，法兰克人正以同样的方式对待这些被他们统称为“撒克逊人”的民族。

sentences.en: So sort of sticking labels on people, very Roman thing to do to kind of classify people and say,
sentences.zh: 所以，给人们贴标签，这是一种非常罗马式的做法，去对人进行分类，然后说，

sentences.en: these are these people and they have red hair and these are their habits and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: “这些人是某某人，他们有红色的头发，这是他们的习惯”，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: On the Franks, the Franks presumably now at this point,
sentences.zh: 关于法兰克人，法兰克人大概现在在这个阶段，

sentences.en: Charlemagne very much sees himself as the heir, doesn't he, to the Roman inheritance, do you think?
sentences.zh: 查理曼非常把自己看作是罗马遗产的继承人，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I think he does.
sentences.zh: 我想他是的。

sentences.en: I mean, not actually to Augustus, but to the Christian emperors who had ruled a great Christian realm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不是奥古斯都的继承人，而是那些统治过伟大基督教王国的基督教皇帝的继承人。

sentences.en: And of course, that is one point of difference between Charlemagne and Augustus is that Charlemagne is, you know, he's not just a great conqueror, but he is a Christian conqueror.
sentences.zh: 当然，查理曼和奥古斯都之间的一个区别点在于，查理曼不仅是一位伟大的征服者，而且是一位基督教征服者。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of quality of paradox to that because there hasn't really been such a figure before.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一种悖论，因为之前并没有出现过这样的人物。

sentences.en: So when he advances into the lands of the Saxons, he's not aiming just to conquer them.
sentences.zh: 所以当他进入撒克逊人的土地时，他的目的不仅仅是征服他们。

sentences.en: He wants to save their souls.
sentences.zh: 他想要拯救他们的灵魂。

sentences.en: He wants to bring them to ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 他想要引领他们皈依基督。

sentences.en: And this great shrine that I described Charlemagne as destroying in 772, it's not just that it's rich.
sentences.zh: 我描述的查理曼在772年摧毁的那座伟大的神殿，不仅仅是因为它富有。

sentences.en: It's obviously the fact that it is a pagan shrine.
sentences.zh: 显然是因为它是一座异教神殿。

sentences.en: It's fearsome.
sentences.zh: 它令人敬畏。

sentences.en: It's phallic.
sentences.zh: 它带有生殖崇拜的意味。

sentences.en: It's basically a massive great pole sticking up out of the Saxon earth, famed across Saxony and believed by the Saxons to uphold the very heavens themselves.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一根巨大的柱子，从撒克逊的土地上拔地而起，在整个萨克森地区闻名遐迩，被撒克逊人认为是支撑着整个天穹。

sentences.en: And so Charlemagne chops it down to demonstrate that this isn't true, that it has no sacral potency whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 所以查理曼把它砍倒，以证明这不是真的，它没有任何神圣的力量。

sentences.en: And I guess even the looting of its treasures can be justified in terms of what churchmen in Charlemagne's realm are coming to describe as a process of correctio.
sentences.zh: 我想，即使是掠夺它的财宝，也可以用查理曼领地内的教会人士所描述的“纠正”过程来辩解。

sentences.en: So it's a Latin word, which means the bringing of order where there is disorder, burnishing what has been besmeared and besmirched.
sentences.zh: 这是一个拉丁词，意思是将秩序带到混乱之处，擦亮那些被玷污和弄脏的东西。

sentences.en: And can I at this point quote for myself for a millennium?
sentences.zh: 我可以在这里引用我为千年所写的内容吗？

sentences.en: Do.
sentences.zh: 请便。

sentences.en: So this program, here was a program to whet the ambitions of warlords as well as scholars and to send men into battle beneath the fluttering of banners,
sentences.zh: 所以这个计划，这是一个旨在激发军阀和学者野心的计划，让人们在旗帜飘扬、

sentences.en: the hiss of arrows and the shadow of carrion crows quite as much as into the mildewed quiet of libraries.
sentences.zh: 箭矢呼啸和食腐乌鸦的阴影下投入战斗，就像投入图书馆那发霉的宁静中一样。

sentences.en: And is that you or is that Paulinus?
sentences.zh: 那是你写的还是保利努斯写的？

sentences.en: Well, very hard to tell us apart, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想很难把我们区分开来。

sentences.en: You can see that he's been a great influence on my prose.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出他对我散文风格的影响很大。

sentences.en: But there is this idea that Charlemagne cleaves to very, very passionately, that in bringing sword and fire to the lands of the Saxons,
sentences.zh: 但查理曼非常热衷于这样一个理念：在给撒克逊人的土地带来刀剑与战火的同时，

sentences.en: he is also bringing order and essentially it's all for their own good.
sentences.zh: 他也在带来秩序，从本质上讲，这一切都是为了他们好。

sentences.en: It's all for their own benefit.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了他们的利益。

sentences.en: But Saxony is not the only place that he's looking at, is he?
sentences.zh: 但萨克森并不是他唯一关注的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he's looking beyond the frontiers of what was once Gaul, which is now Francia.
sentences.zh: 因为他的目光超越了曾经的高卢，也就是现在的法兰克王国的边境。

sentences.en: And he's also looking to Italy, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他也在关注意大利，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, you know, Italy is still a bit of a lodestar for people who are living in the ruins of the Roman Empire, the inheritance of Rome and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，对于那些生活在罗马帝国废墟中、继承了罗马遗产的人来说，意大利仍然是一个指路明灯。

sentences.en: So what's going on in Italy?
sentences.zh: 那么意大利发生了什么？

sentences.en: Italy is now under the sway of the Lombards.
sentences.zh: 意大利现在处于伦巴第人的统治之下。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, in the previous episode, we heard how the Pope in Rome, he had anointed Charlemagne's father, thereby providing him with the religious legitimacy that he wanted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在上一集中，我们听到了罗马教皇是如何为查理曼的父亲涂油加冕的，从而为他提供了他想要的宗教合法性。

sentences.en: So it's become very important to the Carolingians.
sentences.zh: 所以这对加洛林王朝变得非常重要。

sentences.en: The papacy basically has licensed them to become kings.
sentences.zh: 教皇基本上授权他们成为国王。

sentences.en: So a very important figure.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常重要的人物。

sentences.en: But he's been menaced by the Lombards.
sentences.zh: 但他一直受到伦巴第人的威胁。

sentences.en: And essentially, the quid pro quo between the Carolingians and the papacy is that the Pope will, you know, anoint kings and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，加洛林王朝和教皇之间的交换条件是，教皇会为国王涂油加冕，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, the Carolingians are expected to keep the Lombards, who are these very impotent people in the north of Italy, keep them on a kind of tight leash.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，加洛林王朝被期望去控制伦巴第人，这些在意大利北部非常无能的人，要严加管束。

sentences.en: And Charlemagne, whose ambitions are clearly considerable in a way that not even his fathers had been,
sentences.zh: 而查理曼，他的野心显然很大，甚至超过了他的父亲，

sentences.en: even when he's in Saxony, is thinking about what could I do against the Lombards?
sentences.zh: 即使当他在萨克森时，他也在思考：我能对伦巴第人做些什么？

sentences.en: I mean, maybe I could just swallow up their kingdom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许我可以吞并他们的王国。

sentences.en: And so when he strips this great pagan shrine of all its treasure, I think he is thinking, you know, this is great.
sentences.zh: 所以当他剥夺了这座伟大异教神殿的所有财宝时，我想他在想，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I can use this to essentially fund a war against the Lombards.
sentences.zh: 我可以利用这些财宝来资助一场针对伦巴第人的战争。

sentences.en: And he will need it because the Lombards occupy a stretch of land that is dotted, as you said, with ancient Roman cities that have walls that are impressive.
sentences.zh: 他会需要这些钱，因为伦巴第人占据的一片土地上，正如你所说，点缀着古老的罗马城市，这些城市有着令人印象深刻的城墙。

sentences.en: The Lombards are a kingdom a bit like the Franks.
sentences.zh: 伦巴第人是一个有点像法兰克人的王国。

sentences.en: I mean, on a smaller scale, but kind of a challenge of a different order to the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，规模较小，但对撒克逊人来说，这是一种不同量级的挑战。

sentences.en: And they're also Germanic.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也是日耳曼人。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: The Lombards?
sentences.zh: 伦巴第人吗？

sentences.en: They are Germanic.
sentences.zh: 他们是日耳曼人。

sentences.en: They command the Alpine passes.
sentences.zh: 他们控制着阿尔卑斯山的山口。

sentences.en: So that's a potential problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个潜在的问题。

sentences.en: And there is also bad blood between Charlemagne and the Lombard king, who's a man called Desiderius, because Charlemagne had been married to the daughter of Desiderius for a year
sentences.zh: 而且查理曼大帝和伦巴第国王德西德里乌斯之间也积怨已久，因为查理曼曾娶了德西德里乌斯的女儿为妻，维持了一年时间，

sentences.en: and then basically had dumped her.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上就把她给休了。

sentences.en: I think for diplomatic reasons rather than personal reasons, because he needed to marry someone else from Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 我想这是出于外交原因而非个人原因，因为他需要娶一位来自中欧的女子。

sentences.en: And Desiderius also is harboring a rival claimant to the throne of Francia.
sentences.zh: 而且德西德里乌斯还窝藏着法兰克王位的竞争对手。

sentences.en: So basically, when this bloke died of a nosebleed,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，当那个家伙因流鼻血而死时，

sentences.en: Charlemagne's brother, Karlamann, his wife and sons had gone off and taken refuge with the Lombards, hadn't they?
sentences.zh: 查理曼的兄弟卡洛曼，他的妻子和儿子们不是已经逃走并投奔了伦巴第人吗？

sentences.en: So that's a bit of a worry for Charlemagne, that the wife and the sons are hanging around in what's now Lombardy.
sentences.zh: 所以这对查理曼来说是个心头大患，因为他的妻子和儿子们正待在现在的伦巴第地区。

sentences.en: Well, I think that is probably actually the biggest consideration of all, because Charlemagne knows that the one thing that could really cripple his offensive capacity
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这可能确实是所有考量中最重要的一个，因为查理曼知道，唯一能真正削弱他进攻能力

sentences.en: and the integrity of his empire is kind of factional rivalry with rival members of his own family.
sentences.zh: 以及帝国完整性的，就是他家族内部成员之间的派系斗争。

sentences.en: And we know that this is weighing on his mind, because we have a life of Hadrian I, who's become Pope shortly after Charlemagne's come to power.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这让他忧心忡忡，因为我们有哈德良一世的传记，他在查理曼掌权后不久就当上了教皇。

sentences.en: And in this biography, it says that the wife and sons of the late Karlamann king of the Franks had taken refuge with Desiderius, who was trying hard to make good his contention,
sentences.zh: 在这部传记中写道，已故法兰克国王卡洛曼的妻子和儿子们投奔了德西德里乌斯，而德西德里乌斯正极力想要证实他的主张，

sentences.en: that these princes should assume the kingship of the Franks in the hope of stirring up dissensions in the kingdom of the Franks.
sentences.zh: 即这些王子应该继承法兰克王位，以期在法兰克王国中煽动纷争。

sentences.en: And in fact, Desiderius writes to the Pope and says, look, I've got these two boys, crown them, anoint them, give them your legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，德西德里乌斯写信给教皇说，看，我这里有两个男孩，给他们加冕，给他们涂圣油，赋予他们你的合法性。

sentences.en: Hadrian refuses because he essentially has to weigh up which of these two guys is likelier to win.
sentences.zh: 哈德良拒绝了，因为他本质上必须权衡这两个人中谁更有可能获胜。

sentences.en: And he decides that Charlemagne is the likelier.
sentences.zh: 他认为查理曼更有可能。

sentences.en: But he's still in an awkward position because Desiderius is between him and Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 但他仍处于尴尬的境地，因为德西德里乌斯就在他和查理曼之间。

sentences.en: And in fact, when Hadrian sends a messenger to Charlemagne saying, please come to my rescue, I'm being menaced.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当哈德良派信使去查理曼那里说，请来救救我，我正受到威胁时，

sentences.en: He can't actually use the Alpine passes because they've been shut off.
sentences.zh: 他实际上无法使用阿尔卑斯山的山口，因为它们已经被封锁了。

sentences.en: And so he has to send the messenger via Marseille, which then goes up to Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 所以他不得不通过马赛派信使，然后再传达给查理曼。

sentences.en: And when Charlemagne gets this message, it confirms his worst anxieties, essentially that Desiderius will be using these two nephews to strike at him.
sentences.zh: 当查理曼收到这个消息时，证实了他最担心的事，即德西德里乌斯会利用这两个侄子来攻击他。

sentences.en: And so he thinks, OK, I've got to go to war.
sentences.zh: 所以他想，好吧，我必须开战了。

sentences.en: So the summer of 773, Charles summons his peers, his warriors, his advisors, to Geneva in Switzerland, holds a great council there.
sentences.zh: 于是在773年夏天，查理召集了他的贵族、战士和顾问到瑞士日内瓦，在那里举行了一场盛大的会议。

sentences.en: You know, he wants to get the support of his followers for the war that's to come.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他想为即将到来的战争争取追随者的支持。

sentences.en: And then having got that, he advances southwards.
sentences.zh: 在得到支持后，他向南推进。

sentences.en: He seizes control of the two main mountain passes over the Alps.
sentences.zh: 他夺取了阿尔卑斯山两条主要山口的控制权。

sentences.en: And once he's done that, he then sends ambassadors to Desiderius.
sentences.zh: 一旦做到这一点，他就派使者去见德西德里乌斯。

sentences.en: And you can see what his main target is.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出他的主要目标是什么。

sentences.en: Because even at this point, his prime anxiety is to get hold of the nephews.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在这一点上，他最焦虑的还是抓住那两个侄子。

sentences.en: And he says to Desiderius, look, I am willing to hold off war.
sentences.zh: 他对德西德里乌斯说，看，我愿意推迟战争。

sentences.en: And I'm willing to pay you a frankly enormous amount of money if you will hand these boys over to me.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把这两个男孩交给我，我愿意付给你一笔坦白说非常巨大的钱。

sentences.en: And Desiderius refuses.
sentences.zh: 但德西德里乌斯拒绝了。

sentences.en: And Charlemagne, I think, is really quite surprised by this.
sentences.zh: 我想查理曼对此确实感到相当惊讶。

sentences.en: Janet Nelson, in her brilliant biography of Charlemagne, offers an explanation for why Desiderius should have refused Charlemagne's offer.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特·纳尔逊在她那本精彩的查理曼传记中，对德西德里乌斯为何拒绝查理曼的提议做出了解释。

sentences.en: She writes, Charles underestimated one thing that was beyond price, the Lombard king's honor.
sentences.zh: 她写道，查理低估了一样无价的东西，那就是伦巴第国王的荣誉。

sentences.en: What father does deals with the man who has repudiated his daughter?
sentences.zh: 哪位父亲会与那个休了自己女儿的男人做交易呢？

sentences.en: And she speaks the truth there.
sentences.zh: 她在这一点上说得很对。

sentences.en: Do you think that's plausible?
sentences.zh: 你认为这合理吗？

sentences.en: I mean, Charlemagne is a man of realpolitik.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，查理曼是一个现实政治家。

sentences.en: And so is Desiderius.
sentences.zh: 德西德里乌斯也是。

sentences.en: Do you think Desiderius really is thinking, oh, I'm just really bitter about this family row.
sentences.zh: 你认为德西德里乌斯真的在想，哦，我只是对这场家庭纠纷耿耿于怀吗？

sentences.en: And that's the single biggest thing in his decision making.
sentences.zh: 那是他决策中最大的因素吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think he thinks, no, I'd rather keep hold of these boys because they're such a powerful political pawn for me?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为他在想，不，我宁愿留住这两个男孩，因为他们对我来说是如此强大的政治筹码？

sentences.en: I think a bit of both.
sentences.zh: 我觉得两者都有。

sentences.en: I think if his honor had not been insulted, perhaps he might have taken the money and settled for peace.
sentences.zh: 我想如果他的荣誉没有受到侮辱，也许他会拿钱并接受和平。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Yes, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: I think the sense that he's been shamed before the eyes of his own people and of Christian Europe generally was clearly very strong.
sentences.zh: 我认为那种在自己的人民和整个基督教欧洲面前蒙羞的感觉显然非常强烈。

sentences.en: And so he decides that he's going to fight.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定要战斗。

sentences.en: And so war breaks out.
sentences.zh: 于是战争爆发了。

sentences.en: Charles descends from the Alps into northern Italy.
sentences.zh: 查理从阿尔卑斯山南下进入意大利北部。

sentences.en: And his immediate target is Pavia, because that is where Desiderius has set himself up.
sentences.zh: 他直接的目标是帕维亚，因为那是德西德里乌斯安顿自己的地方。

sentences.en: But it's also because, according to reports, that is where the two nephews are, the two princes.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为据报道，那两个侄子，也就是那两位王子，就在那里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who I'm sure have been kept in a tower.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定他们被关在塔里。

sentences.en: However, when he gets there,
sentences.zh: 然而，当他到达那里时，

sentences.en: Charlemagne finds that he's too late, that the princes have been sent away to Verona.
sentences.zh: 查理曼发现他来晚了，王子们已经被送往维罗纳了。

sentences.en: And so he splits his forces.
sentences.zh: 于是他分兵了。

sentences.en: So the life of Hadrian, the Pope, we're told Charles left most of his forces at Pavia and with a number of his bravest franks moved rapidly towards Verona.
sentences.zh: 根据教皇哈德良的传记，我们被告知查理将大部分军队留在了帕维亚，并带着他最勇敢的一些法兰克人迅速向维罗纳进发。

sentences.en: And this is a move that clearly takes the defenders of Verona by surprise.
sentences.zh: 这一举动显然让维罗纳的守军措手不及。

sentences.en: And Carloman's sons and his wife, who has the brilliant name of Gerberga, they all surrender themselves to Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 卡洛曼的儿子们和他的妻子，那个有着好名字格贝加的女人，他们都向查理曼投降了。

sentences.en: Although, according to the life of Hadrian,
sentences.zh: 尽管根据哈德良的传记，

sentences.en: Carloman's wives and sons immediately handed themselves over of their own free wills.
sentences.zh: 卡洛曼的妻子和儿子们是立即自愿投降的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but believe that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但谁信呢。

sentences.en: So it sounds slightly like there's some special pleading going on.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点像是在进行某种特殊的辩解。

sentences.en: And the intriguing thing is that from this point on, that is the last dimension of them.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，从那时起，就再也没有关于他们的记载了。

sentences.en: And there were two boys, right?
sentences.zh: 那是两个男孩，对吧？

sentences.en: Two boys.
sentences.zh: 两个男孩。

sentences.en: And the last we heard of them, they're in Verona.
sentences.zh: 我们最后一次听到他们的消息，他们是在维罗纳。

sentences.en: So they ended their lives literally as two gentlemen of Verona.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最终确实成了“维罗纳的两位绅士”。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, they may have been, you know, tonsured.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他们可能，你知道，被剃度了。

sentences.en: So had their hair shaved off and packed off to the monastery.
sentences.zh: 所以头发被剃光，被送进了修道院。

sentences.en: But if they were, we don't hear about it.
sentences.zh: 但如果真是这样，我们也没听说过。

sentences.en: They're probably being killed.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能被杀了。

sentences.en: They've been killed.
sentences.zh: 他们被杀了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, maybe Charlemagne Richard III did.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，也许查理曼像理查三世那样做了。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们不知道。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, that's the end of them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是他们的结局。

sentences.en: What's going on in Pavia?
sentences.zh: 帕维亚那边发生了什么？

sentences.en: The siege there is still continuing, right?
sentences.zh: 那里的围城战还在继续，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right the way through the winter, Desiderius holding out.
sentences.zh: 整个冬天，德西德里乌斯都在坚守。

sentences.en: And Charles seems to have had a slight wobble.
sentences.zh: 而查理似乎有些动摇。

sentences.en: He abandons the siege and he goes south to Rome.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了围攻，南下前往罗马。

sentences.en: So it's his first visit to Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他第一次访问罗马。

sentences.en: And he goes to St. Peter's tomb and he prays there.
sentences.zh: 他去了圣彼得墓前祈祷。

sentences.en: And whether it is for St. Peter to intercede with God to help him in the siege, or maybe, I mean, maybe it's the expression of a guilty conscience.
sentences.zh: 无论是为了让圣彼得向神祈求帮助他围城，还是说，我的意思是，也许这是出于负罪感的表达。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe he feels bad about what he's done to his nephews.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许他对自己对侄子们所做的事感到难过。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: But it's clearly the case that when he goes back to Pavia, his morale has been boosted.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，当他回到帕维亚时，他的士气大振。

sentences.en: He's back in the saddle.
sentences.zh: 他重整旗鼓了。

sentences.en: He's full of vigor.
sentences.zh: 他充满了活力。

sentences.en: And he prosecutes the siege with a kind of renewed sense of aggression.
sentences.zh: 他以一种重新燃起的侵略感继续围城。

sentences.en: And if he was praying for God's assistance, then God gives it because a terrible plague breaks out in Pavia.
sentences.zh: 如果他是在祈求神的帮助，那么神确实给予了，因为帕维亚爆发了一场可怕的瘟疫。

sentences.en: And it causes such devastation that Desiderius basically surrenders.
sentences.zh: 它造成了巨大的破坏，以至于德西德里乌斯基本上投降了。

sentences.en: He has no choice.
sentences.zh: 他别无选择。

sentences.en: So again, quoting from the life of Hadrian, the wrath of God raged and stormed against all the Lombards in that city.
sentences.zh: 所以再次引用哈德良的传记，神的愤怒在那个城市里对所有伦巴第人肆虐。

sentences.en: And they were so enfeebled by disease and death that the excellent king of the Franks captured the city together with Desiderius.
sentences.zh: 他们被疾病和死亡折磨得如此虚弱，以至于这位杰出的法兰克国王连同德西德里乌斯一起占领了这座城市。

sentences.en: And that essentially is the end, not just of Desiderius's ambitions, but of the independence of the Lombard kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这基本上不仅是德西德里乌斯野心的终结，也是伦巴第王国独立的终结。

sentences.en: And Desiderius is taken back to Francia.
sentences.zh: 德西德里乌斯被带回了法兰克。

sentences.en: He is tonsured.
sentences.zh: 他被剃度了。

sentences.en: He is sent to a monastery.
sentences.zh: 他被送进了一座修道院。

sentences.en: And Lombardy, the kingdom isn't erased.
sentences.zh: 而伦巴第，这个王国并没有被抹去。

sentences.en: Charlemagne becomes king of the Lombards.
sentences.zh: 查理曼成为了伦巴第人的国王。

sentences.en: So from this point on, he is described in his charters as king of the Franks and of the
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，他在宪章中被称为法兰克人和伦巴第人的国王。

sentences.en: Lombards.
sentences.zh: 伦巴第人。

sentences.en: But Lombardy is now clearly a part of Charlemagne's empire.
sentences.zh: 但伦巴第现在显然是查理曼帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: And his power now extends right the way to Rome.
sentences.zh: 他的权力现在一直延伸到罗马。

sentences.en: So it's a significant advance of the Frankish frontier.
sentences.zh: 所以这是法兰克边境的重大推进。

sentences.en: And to put that into context, he is the first bloke, presumably, to rule unchallenged in
sentences.zh: 把这一点放在背景中来看，他大概是第一个在

sentences.en: Gaul and certainly the top half of Italy for, what, 200 years, maybe?
sentences.zh: 高卢以及意大利的上半部分统治了，怎么说，200年，也许更久，且无人挑战的人？

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, even longer.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，甚至更久。

sentences.en: I mean, back to the time of the fall of the Roman Empire in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回到西罗马帝国灭亡的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: A person can be drawn into faith, not forced into it.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一封写于796年的信，寄给查理曼随行的一位朝臣，当时他正在狠狠地打击撒克逊人。

sentences.en: A person can be forced into baptism, but that person will not advance in faith unless he be an infant.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在我读那段话前大约四秒钟，你说，哦，拜托，你能用约克郡口音读一下吗？

sentences.en: Even after people have received the faith and baptism, their weaker minds should be offered instruction with gentleness.
sentences.zh: 向听众解释一下你为什么想听那个。

sentences.en: For as the Apostle Paul said when he wrote to his followers among the Galatians, I have fed you not with meat, but with milk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分原因是我一直很喜欢听你的约克郡口音。

sentences.en: So that was a letter written in 796 to a courtier in Charlemagne's train at the time when he's absolutely smiting the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Tom, about four seconds before I was about to read that, you said, oh, please, can you read that in a Yorkshire accent?
sentences.zh: 但也因为那封信的作者来自约克。

sentences.en: Explain to the listeners why you wanted to hear that.
sentences.zh: 他是一个诺森布里亚人，也就是一个叫阿尔昆的盎格鲁-撒克逊人。

sentences.en: Well, partly because I always enjoy hearing your Yorkshire accent.
sentences.zh: 阿尔昆是一位非常杰出的学者，继承了诺森布里亚学术伟大成就的最崇高传统。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以他是比德的弟子教出来的，没错。

sentences.en: But also because the author of that letter was from York.
sentences.zh: 所以在这两个非凡的人之间存在着一种学术联系。

sentences.en: He was a Northumbrian, so an Anglo-Saxon called Alcuin.
sentences.zh: 而艾因哈德，同样是查理曼的传记作者，他认为阿尔昆非常出色。

sentences.en: And Alcuin was a very distinguished scholar in the noblest traditions of the great achievements of Northumbrian scholarship.
sentences.zh: 他形容他是随处可见的最博学的人。

sentences.en: So he had been taught by a disciple of Bede, exactly.
sentences.zh: 阿尔昆令人印象深刻的一点是，他在政治上也做得非常好。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of scholarly link between those two extraordinary people.
sentences.zh: 他算是一位非常有经验的外交官。

sentences.en: And Einhard, again, the biography of Charlemagne, he thought Alcuin was brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以在781年，他被约克主教派去，主教基本上想成为大主教。

sentences.en: He described him as the most learned man to be found anywhere.
sentences.zh: 对此有一些疑问。

sentences.en: And the thing that's impressive about Alcuin is that he's also very, very good at politics.
sentences.zh: 于是阿尔昆前往罗马，去协商确认约克主教实际上就是大主教。

sentences.en: He's kind of a very seasoned diplomat.
sentences.zh: 阿尔昆成功做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So in 781, he gets sent by the Bishop of York, who basically wants to be an archbishop.
sentences.zh: 然后他在回程经过意大利时遇到了查理曼。

sentences.en: And there's some doubt about this.
sentences.zh: 查理曼对他非常热情，说，请留下来陪我，留在我的宫廷里。

sentences.en: And so Alcuin goes to Rome to negotiate the absolute confirmation that the Bishop of York is actually an archbishop.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，查理曼不仅是一位非常成功且有时残酷的军阀，也是一个致力于学习、学术的人，

sentences.en: And Alcuin succeeds in doing that.
sentences.zh: 致力于拓宽自己和他人民的文化视野。

sentences.en: And then he's going back through Italy when he runs into Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 随后他在返回意大利的途中偶遇了查理曼大帝。

sentences.en: And Charlemagne is all over him and says, please come and stay with me, stay in my court.
sentences.zh: 查理曼对他非常热情，恳请他留下来，住在自己的宫廷里。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that Charlemagne, as well as being a very successful and on occasion brutal warlord, is also a man who is devoted to learning, to scholarship,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，查理曼不仅是一位成就卓著、有时甚至有些残暴的军阀，同时也是一位致力于学习和学术研究的人，

sentences.en: to kind of broadening the cultural horizons of himself and of his people.
sentences.zh: 他热衷于拓展自己及其子民的文化视野。

sentences.en: And he essentially, he wants a teacher.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是想要一位老师。

sentences.en: And Alcuin is a brilliant teacher.
sentences.zh: 而阿尔昆正是一位杰出的老师。

sentences.en: And so he stays at Charlemagne's side.
sentences.zh: 所以他留在了查理曼身边。

sentences.en: He goes back to England for a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 他回英国待了几年。

sentences.en: But otherwise, he stays in Francie from this point onwards.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，从那时起他就一直待在法兰克。

sentences.en: And from his letters, you can see he's a bit scared of Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 从他的信件中可以看出，他其实有点怕查理曼。

sentences.en: He's a bit nervous of him.
sentences.zh: 他对他有点敬畏。

sentences.en: But they do seem to have become genuinely good friends.
sentences.zh: 但他们看起来确实成了真正的挚友。

sentences.en: So Charlemagne has this massive bath complex and they hang out in the baths together, kind of, you know, making jokes about Virgil.
sentences.zh: 查理曼有一个巨大的浴场建筑群，他们常在那里一起消磨时光，你知道的，还会开些关于维吉尔的玩笑。

sentences.en: And Alcuin's a great japester.
sentences.zh: 阿尔昆是个很爱开玩笑的人。

sentences.en: He's a great one for a nickname.
sentences.zh: 他特别擅长给人起绰号。

sentences.en: So he calls Charlemagne, perhaps tellingly, David, you know, as in King David.
sentences.zh: 所以他称呼查理曼为“大卫”，这或许很有深意，就像圣经里的那位大卫王一样。

sentences.en: And it's all great banter.
sentences.zh: 他们之间总是充满欢声笑语。

sentences.en: And they get on tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 他们相处得非常融洽。

sentences.en: And Alcuin is by Charlemagne's side pretty continuously throughout this period.
sentences.zh: 在那段时期，阿尔昆几乎一直陪伴在查理曼左右。

sentences.en: And then in 796, he's quite elderly by this point.
sentences.zh: 到了796年，他那时已经相当年迈了。

sentences.en: I think he's about 60.
sentences.zh: 我想他当时大约60岁。

sentences.en: He retires to Tor, which, of course, is the great shrine of St. Martin.
sentences.zh: 他隐退到了图尔，那当然是圣马丁的伟大圣地。

sentences.en: So it's the most significant of all the Frankish shrines.
sentences.zh: 那是所有法兰克圣地中最重要的一处。

sentences.en: And there he becomes the abbot.
sentences.zh: 他在那里成为了修道院院长。

sentences.en: But he continues to take an interest, obviously, in what's going on beyond the walls of the monastery.
sentences.zh: 但他显然依然关心着修道院围墙之外发生的事情。

sentences.en: And in 796, you know, which is the year that he's gone to Tor, there is one thing more than anything else that is worrying Alcuin.
sentences.zh: 在796年，也就是他前往图尔的那一年，有一件事比其他任何事都让阿尔昆感到担忧。

sentences.en: And essentially, it's Charlemagne's policy in the East, his policy to the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 本质上，那就是查理曼在东方的政策，他对萨克森人的政策。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is because he thinks Charlemagne's let himself down a bit by being so savage, by being so repressive.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他认为查理曼表现得如此残暴、如此高压，这让他自己也显得有些失格。

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Essentially, yes.
sentences.zh: 本质上，是的。

sentences.en: It's because what Charlemagne is doing is a very radical policy.
sentences.zh: 因为查理曼所做的是一种非常激进的政策。

sentences.en: It's not something that Christian kings and emperors have been in the habit of doing, kind of imposing conversion at the point of a sword.
sentences.zh: 这并不是基督教国王和皇帝们习惯的做法，即用刀剑强迫他人改宗。

sentences.en: People may have a vague sense that this is all that medieval kings did.
sentences.zh: 人们可能隐约觉得这就是中世纪国王所做的一切。

sentences.en: But, you know, certainly in the early Middle Ages and even back in the final years of the Christian emperor, this wasn't what was happening.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，至少在早期中世纪，甚至追溯到基督教皇帝统治的最后几年，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: Because the Roman assumption, which the Franks, I mean, seem to have inherited, is basically that to have faith in Christ is both a kind of a marker and a perk of being civilized.
sentences.zh: 因为罗马人的假设——法兰克人似乎也继承了这一点——基本上是认为信仰基督既是文明的标志，也是文明带来的好处。

sentences.en: And the Christian god is so powerful.
sentences.zh: 而且基督教的上帝如此强大。

sentences.en: Why would you want to share him with your enemies?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要和敌人分享他呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it's much better to keep him for yourself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，把他留给自己要好得多。

sentences.en: But I think that the longer that Charlemagne fights the Saxons, the more obdurate the Saxons seem to be,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，查理曼与萨克森人作战的时间越长，萨克森人似乎就越顽固，

sentences.en: the more he comes to think that his enemies are fighting in the shadow of demons.
sentences.zh: 他就越认为他的敌人是在恶魔的阴影下作战。

sentences.en: That he is making war not just against the Saxons themselves, but against these monstrous demons that they worship.
sentences.zh: 他不仅是在与萨克森人本身作战，也是在与他们所崇拜的那些可怕的恶魔作战。

sentences.en: And that therefore, you know, he will never defeat the Saxons until he has also banished these terrifying and demonic gods from their lands.
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道，除非他能将这些恐怖的恶魔神灵从他们的土地上驱逐出去，否则他永远无法击败萨克森人。

sentences.en: So, in addition to his military strategy, he imposes this strategy essentially of trying to wipe paganism out with extreme prejudice.
sentences.zh: 所以，除了军事战略外，他本质上还实施了一种试图以极端偏见彻底消灭异教的策略。

sentences.en: So, in 776, Charlemagne imposes a treaty on the Saxons that obliges them to accept baptism.
sentences.zh: 因此，在776年，查理曼强迫萨克森人签订了一项条约，要求他们接受洗礼。

sentences.en: They don't have any choice.
sentences.zh: 他们别无选择。

sentences.en: And there's this kind of mass baptism in the River Lippe, kind of thousands and thousands are baptized.
sentences.zh: 当时在利珀河发生了大规模的洗礼，成千上万的人受洗。

sentences.en: But then, of course, the moment he's gone, they all revert.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他一离开，他们就全都反悔了。

sentences.en: And this then seems apostasy and Charlemagne is made even more furious.
sentences.zh: 这被视为背教，查理曼因此更加愤怒。

sentences.en: And so, it becomes a kind of hideous cycle.
sentences.zh: 于是，这变成了一种可怕的循环。

sentences.en: In 785, he pronounces that scorning to come to baptism, so refusing the offer of baptism, will henceforward merit death.
sentences.zh: 785年，他宣布蔑视洗礼，即拒绝接受洗礼的提议，从此以后将被处死。

sentences.en: And he also lists a whole host of other practices that have been part of Saxon traditional way of life for goodness how long.
sentences.zh: 他还列举了许多其他做法，这些做法在萨克森人的传统生活中已经存在了不知多久。

sentences.en: And these two are capital offenses, so offering sacrifice to demons, as Charlemagne describes it, cremation, so you're not allowed to do that, you have to bury your body,
sentences.zh: 这些也被列为死罪，比如向恶魔献祭（正如查理曼所描述的那样）、火葬（这是不允许的，你必须土葬），

sentences.en: or eating meat during Lent, say the 40 days before Easter.
sentences.zh: 或者在四旬斋期间（即复活节前的40天）吃肉。

sentences.en: And this is by miles the most brutal program for bringing a people to Christ that anyone has ever attempted.
sentences.zh: 这是有史以来任何人尝试过的最残酷的让人们皈依基督的计划。

sentences.en: And this is why Alcuin objects to it.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿尔昆反对它的原因。

sentences.en: You know, he feels that this is not what a Christian king should be doing at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他觉得这根本不是一个基督教国王应该做的事。

sentences.en: And I think what sharpens this sense for Alcuin is that he is an Anglo-Saxon.
sentences.zh: 我认为让阿尔昆产生这种强烈感觉的原因是他是一位盎格鲁-撒克逊人。

sentences.en: And the Anglo-Saxons remember how they had been converted, which is essentially by the example and the inspiration of holy men, not warriors.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人记得他们是如何皈依的，本质上是靠圣徒的榜样和感召，而不是靠武士。

sentences.en: So whether it's Irish monks in the north who convert Northumbria, or the missionaries sent from Rome under Augustine, who founds the Archbishopric in Canterbury.
sentences.zh: 无论是北方那些使诺森布里亚皈依的爱尔兰僧侣，还是奥古斯丁从罗马派遣的传教士，后者在坎特伯雷建立了大主教区。

sentences.en: And I think the Anglo-Saxons also have a feeling of kinship with the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为盎格鲁-撒克逊人对萨克森人也有种亲缘感。

sentences.en: There's a sense that, you know, they're cousins.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，你知道，他们是表亲。

sentences.en: Of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: And so this had been an inspiration for a lot of Anglo-Saxon missionaries over the course of the 8th century to go to pagan Germany.
sentences.zh: 因此，这激励了许多盎格鲁-撒克逊传教士在8世纪期间前往异教徒统治的德国。

sentences.en: So we talked about one of them in the previous episode, Boniface, from Devon.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集谈到了其中一位，来自德文郡的博尼法斯。

sentences.en: And Boniface had gone out there and he'd certainly given no quarter to paganism.
sentences.zh: 博尼法斯去了那里，他对异教确实毫不留情。

sentences.en: So like Charlemagne, he had been confronted with a great holy tree that had been sacred to Thor.
sentences.zh: 就像查理曼一样，他也曾面对过一棵对托尔神来说神圣无比的参天大树。

sentences.en: And he'd chopped it down and turned it into a church.
sentences.zh: 他把它砍倒并改建成了一座教堂。

sentences.en: But the thing about Boniface is he does this without kind of mailed men at his back.
sentences.zh: 但博尼法斯的特别之处在于，他做这些事时身后并没有披甲执锐的士兵。

sentences.en: He is doing it as someone who is not carrying weapons.
sentences.zh: 他是一个手无寸铁的人。

sentences.en: And even though Boniface was sponsored by Charles Martel, he never turns to the Frankish, you know, warlord and says, can you give me some men?
sentences.zh: 尽管博尼法斯得到了查理·马特的资助，但他从未转向那位法兰克军阀说：“你能给我派些人吗？”

sentences.en: The whole point is that if you are confronted by armed warriors, then you allow them to cut you down.
sentences.zh: 重点在于，如果你面对的是武装战士，那么你就任由他们砍杀。

sentences.en: And this is what actually happens to Boniface.
sentences.zh: 而这正是博尼法斯最终的结局。

sentences.en: So in 754, he's hacked to death by Frisian pirates.
sentences.zh: 754年，他被弗里斯兰海盗乱刀砍死。

sentences.en: The prayer book that he had in his hand in which he held up to try and stop the blow of the sword gets cuts all the way through it and is preserved as a holy relic.
sentences.zh: 他手中拿着试图抵挡剑击的祈祷书被完全砍穿，并作为圣物保存了下来。

sentences.en: And it's an example to Christians of how you should properly convert pagans.
sentences.zh: 这对基督徒来说是一个关于如何正确感化异教徒的榜样。

sentences.en: You shouldn't be going in and, you know, massacring them and burning villages and things.
sentences.zh: 你不应该冲进去屠杀他们、焚烧村庄之类的。

sentences.en: This is Alcuin's feeling.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿尔昆的感受。

sentences.en: So when Alcuin, he looks at this, he tells Charlemagne, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以当阿尔昆看到这些时，他告诉了查理曼，不是吗？

sentences.en: He has this image of an infant being given milk.
sentences.zh: 他用了婴儿喝奶的比喻。

sentences.en: Yeah, he loves that.
sentences.zh: 是的，他很喜欢那个比喻。

sentences.en: Let peoples newly brought to Christ be nourished in a mild manner as infants are given milk.
sentences.zh: 让新近皈依基督的人民像婴儿喝奶一样，以温和的方式得到滋养。

sentences.en: If you instruct them brutally, the risk then, their minds being weak, is they will vomit everything up.
sentences.zh: 如果你粗暴地教导他们，由于他们心智尚弱，风险就是他们会把一切都吐出来。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a pretty bold thing to write to this guy who's so powerful,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对一个如此强大的人写下这些话是非常大胆的，

sentences.en: to basically say your entire policy is misguided and is actually counterproductive because they will vomit back up the faith that you're forcing down their throats.
sentences.zh: 基本上是说你整个政策都是误导性的，实际上适得其反，因为他们会把你强塞给他们的信仰吐出来。

sentences.en: Yeah, and of course, unspoken is also the thought that, you know, you are going against God's will in doing this.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，言外之意也是你这样做违背了上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: And I agree, it is brave of Alcuin to do it.
sentences.zh: 我同意，阿尔昆这样做很勇敢。

sentences.en: I mean, they may hang out in the baths and, you know, banter, but Charlemagne is still a very intimidating figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可能在浴场里消磨时光、开玩笑，但查理曼仍然是一个非常令人生畏的人物。

sentences.en: But Alcuin does write to him.
sentences.zh: 但阿尔昆确实写信给他了。

sentences.en: And what's amazing is that Charlemagne seems to have taken it on the chin.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，查理曼似乎接受了这些建议。

sentences.en: So that same year, 796, he orders the program of forcible baptisms to be eased.
sentences.zh: 同年，即796年，他下令放宽强制洗礼的计划。

sentences.en: And then the following year, he issues a new charter for the Saxons, kind of easing off the prescriptions.
sentences.zh: 第二年，他为萨克森人颁布了一项新宪章，放宽了那些规定。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say making the laws against paganism more liberal.
sentences.zh: 我不会说这是让反异教法律变得更自由。

sentences.en: That would be an anachronistic way of putting it, but making them slightly less punitive, I guess.
sentences.zh: 那样说会显得不合时宜，但我想说是让它们稍微没那么严苛了。

sentences.en: So Alcuin's take is that essentially you should rely on monasteries rather than on kind of military forts to pacify the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔昆的观点是，本质上你应该依靠修道院而不是军事堡垒来安抚萨克森人。

sentences.en: Charlemagne doesn't go that far.
sentences.zh: 查理曼并没有做到那一步。

sentences.en: You know, he continues to harry and burn and whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他继续骚扰、焚烧等等。

sentences.en: But I think there is a sense in which the monasteries that are built in the kind of the rear of the Saxons and which Charlemagne starts to plant over the eastern reaches of his kingdom.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在某种意义上，那些建在萨克森人后方、查理曼开始在他王国东部领土上建立的修道院，

sentences.en: I mean, they have been compared by scholars to the great Roman legionary bases.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，学者们将它们与伟大的罗马军团基地进行了比较。

sentences.en: You know, these are centers of Christian power from which Christianity can reach outwards and spread eastwards.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些是基督教权力的中心，基督教可以从这里向外延伸并向东传播。

sentences.en: And in that sense, it kind of perfectly fuses the double meaning of correctio, this Latin word for bringing order where there's disorder,
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，它完美地融合了“纠正”（correctio）的双重含义，这个拉丁词意为在混乱的地方建立秩序，

sentences.en: that it is a matter both for warriors with swords and for scholars and monks with pens.
sentences.zh: 这既是手持刀剑的武士的事，也是手握笔杆的学者和僧侣的事。

sentences.en: So there's this phrase, the Carolingian Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个词叫“加洛林文艺复兴”。

sentences.en: The Carolingians don't think that what they're doing is a renaissance because they think that what they're doing is simply carrying on traditions that reach back to the Christian Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 加洛林王朝的人并不认为他们所做的是一场文艺复兴，因为他们认为自己只是在延续追溯到基督教罗马帝国的传统。

sentences.en: But that things need to be corrected.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情需要被纠正。

sentences.en: And so that's what the program is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是该计划的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: It's not a renaissance.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场文艺复兴。

sentences.en: It's a program of correctio.
sentences.zh: 这是一个“纠正”计划。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And not just among the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是在萨克森人中间。

sentences.en: Charlemagne also believes that his own people worthy of...
sentences.zh: 查理曼也认为他自己的人民值得……

sentences.en: Is correction the right word here?
sentences.zh: “纠正”在这里是合适的词吗？

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: There's this line, let men be chosen for the task of improving knowledge who have the will and ability to learn and also the desire to instruct others.
sentences.zh: 有这样一句话：让那些有学习意愿和能力，以及有教导他人愿望的人被选出来承担提升知识的任务。

sentences.en: So basically, it's a huge pedagogical, educational program among his own people.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这在他自己的人民中是一个巨大的教学和教育计划。

sentences.en: And himself, which is why he had got Alcuin.
sentences.zh: 他自己也是如此，这就是他找来阿尔昆的原因。

sentences.en: You know, he wanted a great teacher by his side.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他想要一位伟大的老师在身边。

sentences.en: And I think the reason for this, it's a bit like, listeners may remember a while ago, we did an episode on Alfred.
sentences.zh: 我认为其原因有点像，听众们可能还记得前段时间我们做过一期关于阿尔弗雷德的节目。

sentences.en: After Alfred's victories over the Vikings, his first aim is to restore the monasteries because he sees learning as fundamental to bringing his people to heaven,
sentences.zh: 在阿尔弗雷德战胜维京人之后，他的首要目标是恢复修道院，因为他认为学习是引导他的人民进入天堂、

sentences.en: to winning them eternal life.
sentences.zh: 赢得永生的根本。

sentences.en: And that is his duty as king.
sentences.zh: 那是他作为国王的职责。

sentences.en: If he doesn't do that, if he doesn't succeed in bringing the souls under his charge to Christ, then he will answer for it at the day of judgment.
sentences.zh: 如果他不这样做，如果他不能成功地引导他所管辖的灵魂皈依基督，那么他在审判日将难辞其咎。

sentences.en: And I think the same shadow hangs over Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 我认为同样的阴影也笼罩在查理曼身上。

sentences.en: It's a really urgent, pressing mission for him.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这是一个非常紧迫、迫在眉睫的使命。

sentences.en: So it is kind of education, education, education.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是教育、教育、再教育。

sentences.en: But it's not just education for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是为了教育而教育。

sentences.en: It's about getting his people to heaven.
sentences.zh: 这是为了让他的人民进入天堂。

sentences.en: And that's why I think he's so keen on Alcuin, because he has inherited from his father, Pepin, and his grandfather, Char Martel,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为他如此渴望得到阿尔昆，因为他从父亲丕平和祖父查理·马特那里继承了这样一种观念：

sentences.en: a sense that actually the Anglo-Saxons are best at this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人其实最擅长这类事情。

sentences.en: So Boniface, when he had gone out to convert the pagans, he'd actually also had to work quite hard among the people on the eastern flank of the Frankish Empire,
sentences.zh: 所以博尼法斯在去感化异教徒时，实际上也必须在法兰克帝国东翼的人民中付出很大努力，

sentences.en: who supposedly have been Christian for centuries, because he finds that they're in a terrible state.
sentences.zh: 那些人据称已经信奉基督教几个世纪了，但他发现他们的状况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So he writes of the Frankish clergy, they spend their lives in debauchery, adultery, and every kind of filth.
sentences.zh: 所以他写道，法兰克神职人员的生活沉溺于放荡、通奸和各种污秽之中。

sentences.en: And he's not writing that in any tone of jealousy.
sentences.zh: 他写这些话时并没有任何嫉妒的语气。

sentences.en: He's genuinely very, very, very appalled by this.
sentences.zh: 他是真的对此感到非常、非常、非常震惊。

sentences.en: To be fair, it's what so many English writers down the centuries have said about the French, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 平心而论，几个世纪以来，许多英国作家对法国人都是这么说的，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's the first example, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 那可能是第一个例子。

sentences.en: And the other thing also that's very striking about Anglo-Saxon scholars, when they come to Francia, which was Gaul, a Roman province where people supposedly speak Latin.
sentences.zh: 关于盎格鲁-撒克逊学者还有一点非常引人注目，当他们来到法兰克（即高卢，一个人们据称说拉丁语的罗马行省）时，

sentences.en: The Anglo-Saxon scholars have learned their Latin from books.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊学者是从书本上学习拉丁语的。

sentences.en: They arrive in Gaul, and they find the Latin being spoken by the Franks basically unintelligible.
sentences.zh: 他们到达高卢后，发现法兰克人说的拉丁语基本上听不懂。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that it's on the verge of becoming French.
sentences.zh: 原因在于它正处于演变成法语的边缘。

sentences.en: You know, it's evolving.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在进化。

sentences.en: But to Alcuin and his compadres, it's a sign that the Franks, you know, are hopelessly uneducated, that they've let their inheritance from the Roman slip, and that therefore,
sentences.zh: 但对阿尔昆和他的同伴来说，这标志着法兰克人无可救药地缺乏教育，他们丢掉了罗马人的遗产，因此，

sentences.en: you know, it's not just their morals that need improving, it's also their ability to speak Latin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不仅他们的道德需要改善，他们的拉丁语表达能力也需要提高。

sentences.en: And that matters because to the Anglo-Saxons who had been converted by Roman missionaries,
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为对于那些被罗马传教士感化的盎格鲁-撒克逊人来说，

sentences.en: the association between Christianity and Romanitas is much stronger than it is among the Franks.
sentences.zh: 基督教与“罗马性”之间的联系比在法兰克人中要强得多。

sentences.en: So we talked about this before.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈过这个。

sentences.en: For the Franks, Christianity had always been Gallic.
sentences.zh: 对于法兰克人来说，基督教一直都是高卢式的。

sentences.en: It had always been self-sufficient within Gaul.
sentences.zh: 它在高卢内部一直是自给自足的。

sentences.en: It hadn't looked to Rome for its example.
sentences.zh: 它并没有向罗马寻求榜样。

sentences.en: But for the Anglo-Saxons, Rome is the great example.
sentences.zh: 但对于盎格鲁-撒克逊人来说，罗马是伟大的榜样。

sentences.en: It's a pope who converted them.
sentences.zh: 是教皇感化了他们。

sentences.en: And so the fact that it's an Anglo-Saxon like Alcuin, who is in charge of the most significant monastery in Francia,
sentences.zh: 因此，由像阿尔昆这样一位盎格鲁-撒克逊人来掌管法兰克最重要的修道院，

sentences.en: is really important in integrating Frankish notions of Christianity into a kind of Europe-wide understanding and making it Roman.
sentences.zh: 对于将法兰克的基督教观念整合到一种全欧洲范围的理解中并使其“罗马化”至关重要。

sentences.en: So it's from this point onwards that you really start to have a kind of common Latin Christianity rather than one that is a Christianity that consists of multiple different versions of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是从这一点开始，你才真正开始拥有某种共同的拉丁基督教，而不是那种由多种不同版本组成的基督教。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, one in Rome, one in Gaul, one in wherever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，罗马有一种，高卢有一种，其他地方也各有一种。

sentences.en: And the great powerhouse of this process is Alcuin's Monastery in Tor, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而这一进程的强大推动力是阿尔昆在图尔的修道院，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Tor, obviously, St. Martin, we've heard loads about St. Martin, how important he was for the Franks.
sentences.zh: 所以图尔，显然，圣马丁，我们听过很多关于圣马丁的事，他对于法兰克人来说是多么重要。

sentences.en: So this is a real sort of hub of scholarship.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一个学术中心。

sentences.en: They're copying out all these classical texts to try and improve the standards of Latin.
sentences.zh: 他们正在抄写所有这些古典文本，试图提高拉丁语的标准。

sentences.en: And they're producing all these collections of scripture, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 而且他们正在制作所有这些经文集，不是吗？

sentences.en: So the first, actually, these are the first Bibles.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这些是第一批《圣经》。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Explain to people who may be baffled by that how these could possibly be the first Bibles.
sentences.zh: 给那些可能对此感到困惑的人解释一下，这些怎么可能是第一批《圣经》呢。

sentences.en: So the word Bible comes from the Greek word biblia, which means books.
sentences.zh: “Bible”（圣经）这个词来自希腊语“biblia”，意思是“书”。

sentences.en: And Christian scriptures consist of lots of different books.
sentences.zh: 而基督教经文由许多不同的书组成。

sentences.en: And it had not previously been the habit to gather them within a single text.
sentences.zh: 以前并没有将它们汇编成单一文本的习惯。

sentences.en: But Alcuin is all over this.
sentences.zh: 但阿尔昆对此非常在行。

sentences.en: There is a tradition of doing this, say, in the Northumbrian monasteries.
sentences.zh: 在诺森布里亚的修道院里，有这样做的传统。

sentences.en: And he brings this to Tor.
sentences.zh: 他把这个传统带到了图尔。

sentences.en: And it's from this point on, really, that these collections of books, which are being assembled within the covers, you know, within a single set of covers, start to be known
sentences.zh: 正是从这一点开始，这些被装订在封面内，你知道，装订在同一套封面里的书集，开始被称为

sentences.en: collectively as biblia, i.e. a Bible.
sentences.zh: 统称为“biblia”，即《圣经》。

sentences.en: So it's from this point on that you start to get Bibles.
sentences.zh: 所以正是从这一点开始，你才开始有了《圣经》。

sentences.en: And Alcuin's aim is to get as many of these Bibles out as he possibly can.
sentences.zh: 而阿尔昆的目标是尽可能多地分发这些《圣经》。

sentences.en: And it's actually quite kind of information technology.
sentences.zh: 这实际上有点像信息技术。

sentences.en: There's a monk in Tor.
sentences.zh: 图尔有一位僧侣。

sentences.en: He picks up one of these Bibles, and he's amazed that you get all the different books of the Old Testament and the New Testament in a single text.
sentences.zh: 他拿起其中一本《圣经》，惊讶地发现你可以在单一文本中获得旧约和新约的所有不同书籍。

sentences.en: And he kind of exclaims, this is a library beyond compare.
sentences.zh: 他惊叹道，这是一座无与伦比的图书馆。

sentences.en: And it's a bit like when iPhones or iPads or whatever first came out, that people would say, you know, all the knowledge of the world is on this tiny little tablet, this
sentences.zh: 这有点像iPhone或iPad之类的东西刚出来的时候，人们会说，你知道，世界上所有的知识都在这个小小的平板电脑上，这个

sentences.en: tiny little phone.
sentences.zh: 小小的手机上。

sentences.en: And Alcuin is quite Steve Jobs, because he has a massive emphasis, not just on the volume
sentences.zh: 阿尔昆很像史蒂夫·乔布斯，因为他非常强调，不仅仅是数据量

sentences.en: of data, but also that this data, these books should be easy to use, easy to read, that they should be beautiful, that the production qualities should be completely streamlined.
sentences.zh: 而且这些数据，这些书应该易于使用，易于阅读，它们应该是精美的，生产质量应该完全精简。

sentences.en: And so the Bibles and other books as well that are being produced in the scriptorium at Tor are written to be as user-friendly as possible.
sentences.zh: 因此，在图尔的缮写室里制作的《圣经》和其他书籍，在编写时都尽可能做到用户友好。

sentences.en: And essentially, when you look at a block of text now written in the Roman script, so the script that English and French and German and everything uses, you are looking at a
sentences.zh: 本质上，当你现在看一块用罗马字母书写的文本块时，也就是英语、法语、德语等使用的文字，你看到的是

sentences.en: script that has been mediated by Carolingian scholars, by Alcuin and his fellow monks.
sentences.zh: 一种由加洛林学者、由阿尔昆和他的僧侣同僚们调解过的文字。

sentences.en: So it's under Alcuin's guidance that for the first time, words don't run into one another.
sentences.zh: 所以是在阿尔昆的指导下，单词第一次不再连在一起。

sentences.en: So if you think of a Roman inscription, you know, there's no spaces, but now you start to get spaces, also the use of capitals to indicate new sentences.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到罗马铭文，你知道，没有空格，但现在你开始有了空格，也开始使用大写字母来表示新句子的开始。

sentences.en: Again, a complete innovation.
sentences.zh: 这又是一项彻底的创新。

sentences.en: And my favorite innovation, the Carolingians start to introduce new punctuation marks.
sentences.zh: 而我最喜欢的创新是，加洛林人开始引入新的标点符号。

sentences.en: And in a sentence where there is doubt being expressed, they start to use a kind of lightning flash, which over the course of time will evolve to become the question mark.
sentences.zh: 在一个表达怀疑的句子中，他们开始使用一种闪电符号，随着时间的推移，它演变成了问号。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So again, Alcuin, you know, he's all about the milk of doctrine and all that, but he also, he's the inventor of the Bible and the question mark.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿尔昆，你知道，他一心只想着教义的乳汁之类的东西，但他同时也是《圣经》和问号的发明者。

sentences.en: I'd never thought of a question mark as a lightning bolt over a full stop, but that's of course is kind of what it is, a slightly wobbly lightning bolt.
sentences.zh: 我从来没想过问号是句号上的一道闪电，但那当然就是它的样子，一个稍微有点摇晃的闪电。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So questioning the full stop.
sentences.zh: 所以是在质疑句号。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So they're basically pumping these out, all these Bibles.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是在大量生产这些《圣经》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're readable.
sentences.zh: 它们易于阅读。

sentences.en: They're in a very beautiful, user-friendly kind of format, and they are presumably a tool of uniformity, right?
sentences.zh: 它们采用了一种非常精美、用户友好的格式，而且它们大概是一种统一的工具，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Across Charlemagne's empire.
sentences.zh: 在查理曼大帝的帝国范围内。

sentences.en: That's what he's after.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所追求的。

sentences.en: Yes, he's creating a common Christian culture.
sentences.zh: 是的，他正在创造一种共同的基督教文化。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, texts are for those who can read.
sentences.zh: 当然，文本是给那些识字的人看的。

sentences.en: So these Bibles are kind of going to monasteries or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以这些《圣经》大概是送往修道院之类的。

sentences.en: But Charlemagne and Alcuin are both very, very concerned to reach out into the countryside.
sentences.zh: 但查理曼和阿尔昆都非常、非常关心如何深入到乡村地区。

sentences.en: So people may wonder, it's a long time since Clovis was converted.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能会好奇，克洛维皈依已经是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: The Frankish elites, the aristocracy, all of that are clearly very, very Christian.
sentences.zh: 法兰克精英、贵族阶层，所有这些显然都非常、非常虔诚地信仰基督教。

sentences.en: But what about the peasants out in the countryside?
sentences.zh: 但乡村里的农民呢？

sentences.en: What do they know about it?
sentences.zh: 他们对此了解多少？

sentences.en: Probably very little.
sentences.zh: 可能知之甚少。

sentences.en: And these are the people that Charlemagne is also very, very concerned to reach.
sentences.zh: 而这些人也是查理曼非常、非常关心要触及的对象。

sentences.en: And the key people here are the parish priests.
sentences.zh: 这里的关键人物是教区牧师。

sentences.en: And Boniface had complained about the fact that they're hopeless.
sentences.zh: 博尼法斯曾抱怨说他们无可救药。

sentences.en: They don't know anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都不懂。

sentences.en: And Alcuin also actually says he worries that the priests, they don't really know what they're talking about.
sentences.zh: 阿尔昆也确实说过，他担心牧师们并不真正知道他们在说什么。

sentences.en: And so, again, he devises kind of little books, little format books that can be slipped into
sentences.zh: 所以，他再次设计了一些小书，可以塞进

sentences.en: a pouch or something that give the basics of Christian doctrine, give the Lord's Prayer, give the creed, give various key passages from Scripture or whatever.
sentences.zh: 小袋子之类的东西里，提供基督教教义的基础知识，提供主祷文、信经，提供经文中的各种关键段落等等。

sentences.en: And these are sent out into the parishes, out into the countryside.
sentences.zh: 这些被分发到各个教区，分发到乡村地区。

sentences.en: And it's an unprecedented experiment in the West in mass education.
sentences.zh: 这是西方在大众教育方面史无前例的实验。

sentences.en: And within a few decades, the bishops in Francia are able to assume that priests should have a basic modicum of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 几十年内，法兰克王国的各主教就能假定牧师应该具备基本的知识水平。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's this wonderful account of a priest in about the kind of the 840s who gets imprisoned
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一个关于大约840年代一位牧师的精彩记载，他被他的主教监禁了

sentences.en: by his bishop for having forgotten everything that he had learned, which always kind of sticks in my mind.
sentences.zh: 因为他忘记了他所学的一切，这总是让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, if you got punished for forgetting everything you'd learned, that would be a real problem.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你因为忘记了所学的一切而受到惩罚，那将是一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: And this, again, it's hard to emphasise how significant a moment this is in the history of Western Europe,
sentences.zh: 而且这，再次强调，很难强调这是西欧历史上多么重要的时刻，

sentences.en: because this is the moment when the process of Christianisation really starts to happen.
sentences.zh: 因为这是基督教化进程真正开始发生的时刻。

sentences.en: It's not just for the elites anymore.
sentences.zh: 它不再仅仅是精英阶层的专利了。

sentences.en: It's reaching out into the countryside.
sentences.zh: 它正在深入到乡村地区。

sentences.en: And the most basic rhythms of life, whether it's kind of annual or whether it's from cradle to grave, are starting to be marinated in Christianity.
sentences.zh: 生活中最基本的节奏，无论是年度的，还是从摇篮到坟墓的，都开始被基督教所浸润。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you're drawing up a charter, a legal agreement, if you're tending to a sick animal,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你在起草一份宪章、一份法律协议，如果你在照料一只生病的动物，

sentences.en: if you're working out where you should dig a well, when you should begin the harvest,
sentences.zh: 如果你在考虑应该在哪里挖井，什么时候开始收获，

sentences.en: all of these questions are starting to be framed in Christian terms by priests who have been given the kind of intellectual know-how and ammunition that enables them to do this.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题都开始被那些被赋予了知识和弹药的牧师们用基督教的术语来构建，使他们能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: Yes, because in every village, every town, every hamlet, there is going to be some parish priest or something who sits standing there with this little book.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为在每个村庄、每个城镇、每个小村落，都会有某个教区牧师站在那里，手里拿着这本小书。

sentences.en: You know, this is the prayer for this occasion.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是这个场合的祈祷文。

sentences.en: This is what Jesus would do, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, in a way that wasn't the case 100 or 200 years before this.
sentences.zh: 这就是耶稣会做的事，等等等等，这在100或200年前是不存在的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Charlemagne has described that every priest should know the Lord's Prayer and should know the Creed
sentences.zh: 查理曼曾描述过，每个牧师都应该知道主祷文和信经，

sentences.en: and that they should in turn instruct everybody in his kingdom in the Creed and in the Lord's Prayer.
sentences.zh: 并且他们应该反过来教导他王国里的每个人学习信经和主祷文。

sentences.en: And so that is giving to people kind of fundamentals of familiarity with Christianity that they hadn't previously had.
sentences.zh: 所以这赋予了人们一种他们以前没有的对基督教的基本熟悉感。

sentences.en: And it has a kind of saturating effect.
sentences.zh: 它产生了一种饱和效应。

sentences.en: And the consequences of that are utterly profound for the future of European culture.
sentences.zh: 其后果对欧洲文化的未来极其深远。

sentences.en: It means that people start to take for granted assumptions that are rooted in Christianity
sentences.zh: 这意味着人们开始认为那些植根于基督教的假设是理所当然的，

sentences.en: to the point where they don't even realize, you know, where these assumptions have come from.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们甚至没有意识到，你知道，这些假设是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: And I think it's in this sense that you can call Charlemagne the father of Europe.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是从这个意义上说，你可以称查理曼为欧洲之父。

sentences.en: So this is a phrase that is being applied to him within his own lifetime.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个在他有生之年就被应用在他身上的短语。

sentences.en: I mean, in all kinds of ways, it's a ridiculous thing to call him because, as we will see, his empire actually doesn't last very long.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从各方面来看，称他为这个名字都很荒谬，因为正如我们将看到的，他的帝国实际上并没有持续太久。

sentences.en: But I think in this one sense, the Christianization of people out in the reaches of the countryside, he does deserve that title.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在这一点上，即乡村地区人们的基督教化，他确实配得上这个称号。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But of course, Dominic, father of Europe is not the only title that he will end up with.
sentences.zh: 但当然，多米尼克，欧洲之父并不是他最终获得的唯一头衔。

sentences.en: No, he ends up with a much grander title.
sentences.zh: 不，他最终获得了一个更宏大的头衔。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So maybe we will explore the story of that grander title, his imperial title, in the final episode.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们会在最后一集中探讨那个更宏大头衔的故事，他的帝国头衔。

sentences.en: And because we're feeling festive, Tom, we will explore that story.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们感到节日气氛，汤姆，我们将探讨那个故事。

sentences.en: The climax of this mighty series, it will be out not on Thursday, as usual, but it'll be on Wednesday, Christmas Day, the 25th of December.
sentences.zh: 这个宏大系列的巅峰之作，它不会像往常一样在周四播出，而是在周三，圣诞节，12月25日播出。

sentences.en: And there is actually a very good historical reason for that, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上有一个非常好的历史原因，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which we will explore next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次会探讨。

sentences.en: Because obviously you could listen to it straight away if you're a member of the Rest is History
sentences.zh: 因为显然，如果你是《历史的余味》俱乐部的成员，你可以马上收听。

sentences.en: Club.
sentences.zh: 俱乐部。

sentences.en: And you can always join that club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 你随时可以在therestishistory.com加入那个俱乐部。

sentences.en: But the best time to listen to that episode is definitely going to be Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 但收听那一集的最佳时间绝对是圣诞节当天。

sentences.en: It's one of the most, I read in your notes, one of the most iconic moments in the whole of European history.
sentences.zh: 我在你的笔记里读到，这是整个欧洲历史上最具标志性的时刻之一。

sentences.en: The scene is Rome, the year is AD 800, and the date is Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 场景是罗马，年份是公元800年，日期是圣诞节。

sentences.en: So please join us for that.
sentences.zh: 所以请加入我们。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
